content: Prevotella is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria. The species previously classified as Bacteroides melaninogenicus has been reclassified and divided into two distinct species: Prevotella melaninogenica and Prevotella intermedia. Members of the Prevotella genus are part of the normal flora of the oral cavity and vaginal tract. They are frequently isolated from anaerobic infections of the respiratory tract, including aspiration pneumonia, lung abscesses, pulmonary empyema, chronic otitis media, and sinusitis. Prevotella species have also been identified in abscesses and burns near the oral region, as well as in infections resulting from human bites, paronychia, urinary tract infections, brain abscesses, osteomyelitis, and bacteremia associated with upper respiratory tract infections. These bacteria are particularly prevalent in periodontal disease and periodontal abscesses. In a study examining the gut microbiota of children in Burkina Faso, Africa, Prevotella species accounted for 53% of the gut bacteria. In contrast, these bacteria were absent in age-matched European children. Research has demonstrated that long-term dietary patterns significantly influence the composition of the gut microbiome. Individuals consuming a Western diet rich in protein and animal fats tend to have a predominance of Bacteroides species, whereas those consuming diets high in carbohydrates, particularly fiber, exhibit a dominance of Prevotella species. Prevotella copri has been implicated as a potential contributor to the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis. A recent study on human-derived Prevotella species compared the gene repertoires of bacteria isolated from different human body sites. This study also revealed an open pan-genome, indicating a vast diversity in the gene pool of Prevotella species.
